nodes.n: Rajgarh, 8 AM. The black car is still there. So is something new: Pandey-ji, on a plastic chair, a bat across his knees, staring at it.
Behind him, twelve boys from the nets. And Rocky Bhatia with an ice pack on his knee and a stump in his hand.

msgs.t: Play your match. Nobody is drinking chai here today except us.

nodes.n: Home series. First match. A huddle on the outfield. Fifteen men with their arms locked. You can hear your own heartbeat over eighty thousand people.

nodes.t: Cap number three-oh-seven. Wear it like you earned it. Because you did.
Cap number three-oh-seven. From a chai stall to this huddle. Some of us were handed this. You fought for every thread of it.
...And for the record, I'm glad you were in that tunnel.

nodes.n: He holds out the cap. Navy blue. A small gold star. It weighs nothing. It weighs everything.

nodes.th: Papa. Maa. Pinky. Pandey-ji. Glory Chai. All of it, on my head.

choice.t: Put it on and kiss the star.
Hold it to your chest. Say nothing.

nodes.n: The chase. Nineteen overs gone. You walk out at number six. The noise is a physical thing, like walking into the sea.

moment.title: Debut
moment.desc: Your first ball in the blue cap. Marco Venn, the fastest bowler in the visiting side. Ten off the last over.
moment.winSub: Eighty thousand people learn your name.
moment.loseSub: The crowd still stands for you.

nodes.n: You don't remember the last shot. You remember Vikrant running in from the dugout and nearly knocking you over.
Three runs short. Kabir Sir meets you at the boundary rope. "Good. Now you know what it feels like. Never again."
The dressing room. Music, ice baths, somebody's phone playing your highlights. Karan's phone is face up on the bench next to you. It lights up.
"Lovely debut for the boy. Be a shame if his father's stall caught fire twice."
Karan sees you reading it. Neither of you moves.

nodes.cliff: They're not just watching Papa's stall. They're threatening to burn it. Again.
